newsitem.title: GERMANY: No need to devalue Venezuelan currency - Petkoff.
newsitem.headline: No need to devalue Venezuelan currency - Petkoff.

text.p: Venezuelan Planning Minister Teodoro Petkoff said on Wednesday that he did not believe it was necessary to devalue the country's currency and he expected a slowdown in inflation in late 1996 and in 1997.
"We are not expecting this," he said when asked if he expected the currency, the bolivar, to be devalued.
"The exchange rate has been rather stable recently," he added.
Petkoff also said that he expected monthly inflation for September to be about three to four percent but noted that he expected the rate from June 1996 to June 1997 to be only 22 percent.
That compares with 62 percent from January to June 1996.
For 1997, he said he expected annual inflation of 20 to 25 percent. He also said that he expected non-oil gross domestic produict for 1996 to fall around three to four percent.
He said Venezuelan GDP, including the country's extensive oil industry, would fall about one percent for 1996.
Petkoff said that for 1997 he expected GDP growth of four percent, including the oil industry.
The planning minister had said in London yesterday that he expected Venezuelan monthly inflation to be between two and three percent by the end of the year.
